what_its_for: Alirocumab is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) in your blood. It is used along with a healthy diet and sometimes with other cholesterol-lowering medicines. It may be used if you have heart disease, inherited high cholesterol, or if other cholesterol medicines like statins have not worked well enough or have caused side effects you could not tolerate.
how_to_take: Alirocumab comes as a liquid in a pre-filled pen or syringe that you inject under your skin (subcutaneous injection). You will inject it into your stomach area (abdomen), upper thigh, or upper arm. Do NOT inject into skin that is tender, bruised, red, or hard. Rotate your injection sites each time. Before injecting, let the pen or syringe warm up to room temperature for 30 to 40 minutes — do NOT microwave or heat it. Clean the injection site with an alcohol wipe and let it dry. Follow the step-by-step instructions that come in your package carefully. Ask your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist to show you how to inject it properly before you do it on your own.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 75 mg injected once every 2 weeks. Your doctor may increase your dose to 150 mg every 2 weeks or switch you to 300 mg once every 4 weeks (monthly) depending on how well your cholesterol is controlled. Always follow the exact dose and schedule your doctor prescribes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within 7 days of your missed dose. If it has been more than 7 days, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store alirocumab in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do NOT freeze it. If needed, you can store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 30 days, but keep it away from heat and light. Once stored at room temperature, do not put it back in the refrigerator. Throw away any pen or syringe stored at room temperature that has not been used within 30 days. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens and syringes in an approved sharps container — do not throw them in the regular trash.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods or drinks you must avoid while taking alirocumab. However, continue to follow a heart-healthy, low-fat, low-cholesterol diet as recommended by your doctor. Avoid injecting into the same spot each time to prevent skin irritation. Do not shake the pen or syringe. Do not use it if the liquid looks cloudy, discolored, or contains particles.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: serious allergic reactions such as rash, hives, severe itching, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness. Also contact your doctor if you notice: redness, pain, bruising, or swelling at the injection site that does not go away; new or unusual muscle pain or weakness; confusion or memory problems; or any other symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Alirocumab starts lowering your LDL (bad) cholesterol within about 1 to 2 weeks after your first injection. Your doctor will likely check your cholesterol levels with a blood test about 4 to 8 weeks after you start treatment to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel fine, because high cholesterol usually has no symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy: It is not known if alirocumab is safe to use during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if alirocumab passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Alirocumab is approved for children 8 years and older who have inherited high cholesterol (heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia). Older adults: Alirocumab can generally be used safely in older adults, but always tell your doctor about all your other medicines and health conditions. Kidney or liver disease: Mild to moderate kidney or liver problems usually do not require a dose change, but let your doctor know about any kidney or liver issues.
